q-osmanisches-reich-41#explanation: Mehmed VI fled aboard a British warship in November 1922. His cousin Abdülmecid II remained only caliph until the caliphate, too, was abolished in 1924.
q-osmanisches-reich-42#question: Who led the national movement that abolished the sultanate in 1922?
q-osmanisches-reich-42#explanation: Mustafa Kemal formed a rival government in Ankara and won the War of Independence. The Republic of Turkey was founded in 1923.
q-osmanisches-reich-43#question: What were the recognised religious communities called that largely managed marriage, inheritance and education themselves in the Ottoman Empire?
q-osmanisches-reich-43#explanation: Greek Orthodox Christians, Armenians and Jews lived in such communities under their own religious leaders. They paid a poll tax and were legally disadvantaged.
q-osmanisches-reich-44#choices.0: The selection of the heir among the sultan's sons
q-osmanisches-reich-44#choices.1: The recruitment of Christian boys for the sultan's service
q-osmanisches-reich-44#choices.2: The training of boys as Quran teachers
q-osmanisches-reich-44#choices.3: The ransoming of Christian prisoners of war
q-osmanisches-reich-44#explanation: The boys were converted to Islam and trained as Janissaries or in the palace. Some rose to grand vizier; the architect Sinan also entered state service this way.
q-osmanisches-reich-45#question: What rights did women in the Ottoman Empire have under Islamic law?
q-osmanisches-reich-45#choices.0: They could hold the office of grand vizier
q-osmanisches-reich-45#choices.1: They could own property, inherit and found endowments
q-osmanisches-reich-45#choices.2: They could vote for members of parliament
q-osmanisches-reich-45#explanation: Many upper-class women founded pious endowments for mosques, fountains and soup kitchens. Women could also bring cases to court.
q-osmanisches-reich-46#question: Who published one of the first novels by a woman in Ottoman Turkish in 1892?
q-osmanisches-reich-46#explanation: Fatma Aliye, daughter of Ahmed Cevdet Pasha, championed education and work for Muslim women in articles and books. Since 2009 her portrait has appeared on a Turkish banknote.
q-osmanisches-reich-47#question: What were the capitulations in the Ottoman Empire?
q-osmanisches-reich-47#choices.0: Trade privileges for European states and their merchants
q-osmanisches-reich-47#choices.2: Taxes that Christians and Jews had to pay
q-osmanisches-reich-47#explanation: They granted foreign merchants low customs duties and the jurisdiction of their own consuls, for example France in 1569. In the 19th century they became a tool of European influence and were revoked in 1914.
q-osmanisches-reich-48#question: Which building did the architect Sinan himself regard as his masterpiece?
q-osmanisches-reich-48#choices.1: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque in Istanbul
q-osmanisches-reich-48#explanation: Sinan built the Selimiye Mosque for Selim II when he was around 80. In almost fifty years more than 300 buildings were erected under his direction.
q-osmanisches-reich-49#question: What is Karagöz in Ottoman culture?
q-osmanisches-reich-49#choices.0: An instrument of the Janissary band
q-osmanisches-reich-49#choices.1: A dish of yoghurt and lamb
q-osmanisches-reich-49#choices.2: The main character of the shadow theatre
q-osmanisches-reich-49#choices.3: A dance of the Mevlevi dervishes
q-osmanisches-reich-49#explanation: Shadow puppeteers entertained a wide audience with Karagöz and his counterpart Hacivat, often with wit and criticism of daily life. There were also storytellers and folk poets.
q-osmanisches-reich-50#question: Which of these events happened first?
q-osmanisches-reich-50#explanation: The Battle of Kosovo took place in 1389, the defeat by Timur at Ankara in 1402. Constantinople fell in 1453, and Suleiman won at Mohács in 1526.
q-osmanisches-reich-51#question: On whose side did the Ottoman Empire fight in the First World War?
q-osmanisches-reich-51#explanation: The Young Turk government took the empire into the war alongside Germany in 1914. After the defeat in 1918 the Allies occupied Istanbul.
q-osmanisches-reich-52#question: What task did the debt administration, co-run by European creditors, take over from 1881?
q-osmanisches-reich-52#choices.0: Collecting revenues from salt, tobacco and silk, among others
q-osmanisches-reich-52#choices.1: Appointing the grand vizier and ministers
q-osmanisches-reich-52#choices.3: Administering the holy cities of Mecca and Medina
q-osmanisches-reich-52#explanation: After the state bankruptcy of 1875, Abdülhamid II set up the debt administration by the Decree of Muharrem. The empire thus lost part of its financial independence.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-01#question: Which invention is attributed to Johannes Gutenberg around 1450?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-01#explanatio: In Mainz, Gutenberg developed printing with individually cast letters and a printing press.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-02#question: In which year did Christopher Columbus reach America?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-02#explanatio: Columbus landed on an island in the Bahamas on October 12, 1492.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-03#question: What were Luther's 95 Theses of 1517 directed against first and foremost?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-03#choices.3: Against the translation of the Bible
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-03#explanatio: Luther criticized the practice of buying one's way out of punishment for sin through the purchase of letters of indulgence.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-04#question: Which empire did the Spanish conquer in 1521 with the fall of Tenochtitlan?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-04#explanatio: Tenochtitlan was the capital of the Aztecs; Hernán Cortés conquered it after a siege lasting months.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-05#question: Which innovation did Nicolaus Copernicus advance in his work of 1543?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-05#choices.1: The Earth revolves around the Sun
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-05#explanatio: Copernicus placed the Sun at the center; the elliptical orbits were not discovered until Kepler.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-06#question: What was the purpose of the Council of Trent (1545 to 1563)?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-06#choices.0: The election of a new pope
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-06#choices.3: The clarification of Catholic doctrine in response to the Reformation
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-06#explanatio: The council reaffirmed Catholic doctrine against the Protestants and resolved on internal reforms of the church.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-07#question: What did the Treaty of Tordesillas lay down in 1494?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-07#choices.2: The border between France and the Empire
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-07#choices.3: The division of the world between Spain and Portugal
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-07#explanatio: Along a line in the Atlantic, new lands to the west were to belong to Spain and those to the east to Portugal; this is why Brazil fell to Portugal.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-08#question: Which principle did the Peace of Augsburg of 1555 lay down?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-08#choices.0: The territorial ruler determines the confession of his territory
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-08#choices.1: Every subject freely chooses his religion
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-08#choices.2: Only Catholicism is permitted in the Empire
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-08#choices.3: The emperor decides the faith of all princes
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-08#explanatio: Each imperial estate was allowed to choose between the Catholic and the Lutheran confession for its territory; those of another faith were permitted to emigrate.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-09#question: Which city was a center of learning in the Songhai Empire under Askia Mohammed?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-09#explanatio: Timbuktu on the Niger, with its Sankoré mosque, was a center of Islamic scholarship and of trade across the Sahara.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-10#question: Who founded the Jesuit order in 1540?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-10#explanatio: The former soldier Ignatius of Loyola founded the Society of Jesus, which was confirmed by the pope in 1540.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-11#question: What happened at the Diet of Worms in 1521?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-11#choices.0: Luther refused to recant his teachings
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-11#choices.2: The Peace of Augsburg was concluded
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-11#explanatio: Before Emperor Charles V, Luther declared that he could recant only if he were refuted from the Bible; he was thereupon outlawed.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-12#question: Which ruler governed the Mughal Empire in India from 1556 and was known for his religious tolerance?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-12#explanatio: Akbar abolished the special tax on non-Muslims and had representatives of all religions debate at his court.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-13#question: Which banking family steered the politics of Florence from 1434 without wearing a crown?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-13#explanatio: The Medici skilfully controlled offices, elections and clients and patronised painters, sculptors and architects. The young Michelangelo grew up in the household of Lorenzo de' Medici.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-14#question: Which Augsburg merchant financed the election of Charles V as king in 1519?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-14#explanatio: Jakob Fugger paid for the votes of the prince-electors and controlled copper and silver mining in Tyrol and Hungary. The Fuggers financed popes and emperors.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-15#question: Who described soberly in "The Prince" (1513) how power is won and kept?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-15#explanatio: Machiavelli separated politics from moral ideals and thereby founded modern political thought. He wrote from his experience of the Italian city-states.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-16#question: Who built the dome of Florence Cathedral, consecrated in 1436?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-16#explanatio: Brunelleschi designed a double-shell dome that was built without wooden centring. It is still regarded as the largest brick dome ever built.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-17#question: Which pope commissioned Michelangelo to paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-17#explanatio: Michelangelo painted the ceiling between 1508 and 1512 with over 300 figures, although he saw himself above all as a sculptor. The Last Judgement on the altar wall came later.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-18#question: Which marble statue by Michelangelo was set up in Florence in 1504 and became a symbol of the republic?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-18#explanatio: The figure, over five metres tall, shows the biblical hero in tense calm before the fight. Michelangelo carved it from a block on which other sculptors had failed.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-19#question: Who painted the mural "The Last Supper" in Milan?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-19#explanatio: Leonardo painted The Last Supper in the refectory of a Milan monastery. Besides painting, he studied anatomy, water, flight and mechanics on thousands of notebook pages.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-20#question: Where did Leonardo da Vinci spend the last years of his life until his death in 1519?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-20#choices.2: At the papal court in Rome
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-20#choices.3: At the Medici court in Florence
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-20#explanatio: Leonardo accepted King Francis I's invitation to France. Before that he had worked in Florence, Milan and Rome.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-21#question: In which work did Erasmus of Rotterdam mock monks, theologians and popes in 1511?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-21#explanatio: Erasmus wanted to renew the Church through satire and learning but rejected a split. "Utopia" was written by Thomas More, "The Ship of Fools" by Sebastian Brant.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-22#question: Over which question did Erasmus publicly break with Luther in 1524?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-22#choices.1: The free will of human beings
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-22#explanatio: In his treatise on free will Erasmus contradicted Luther's doctrine of the bondage of the will. He abhorred conflict and violence and remained in the old Church.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-23#question: In which castle did Luther translate the New Testament into German after the Diet of Worms?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-23#explanatio: Elector Frederick the Wise had Luther "kidnapped" for show and hidden at the Wartburg. There he translated the New Testament in just eleven weeks.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-24#question: According to Luther's teaching, how is a person made righteous before God?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-24#explanatio: Luther reached this conviction as a professor of theology in Wittenberg. It was the core of his criticism of indulgences and of piety based on works.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-25#question: What was the name of the list of demands of the rebellious peasants of 1525?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-25#explanatio: In the Twelve Articles of Memmingen the peasants demanded, among other things, the free election of pastors and the end of serfdom. The uprising was crushed in blood.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-26#question: In which city did John Calvin build a strictly regulated Reformed community from 1541?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-26#explanatio: In Geneva church and council jointly supervised faith and conduct. Zurich, by contrast, was Zwingli's city and Wittenberg Luther's.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-27#question: Which doctrine lies at the heart of Calvin's theology?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-27#choices.3: The rebirth of the soul in new lives
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-27#explanatio: According to Calvin, God has destined every person to salvation or damnation. Huguenots, the Dutch, the Scots and the Puritans spread his teaching around the world.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-28#question: What were the French Protestants of Calvinist persuasion called?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-28#explanatio: The Huguenots were persecuted in eight wars of religion, most brutally in the St Bartholomew's Day Massacre of 1572. Puritans, by contrast, were the strict Calvinists in England.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-29#question: Under the influence of which queen mother did the French court have the Huguenot leaders killed in 1572?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-29#explanatio: After a failed attempt on Admiral Coligny's life, the killing of the leaders escalated into the St Bartholomew's Day Massacre. Margaret of Valois was the bride whose wedding had brought the Huguenots to Paris.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-30#question: Which edict granted the Huguenots freedom of worship in 1598 and ended the French Wars of Religion?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-30#explanatio: Henry IV, who had converted to Catholicism, issued the Edict of Nantes. Louis XIV revoked it in 1685 with the Edict of Fontainebleau.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-31#question: Which king separated the English Church from Rome in 1534 and made himself its head?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-31#explanatio: Henry VIII broke with the pope after he refused to annul his first marriage. His daughter Elizabeth I later consolidated the Church of England.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-32#question: Who was the mother of Elizabeth I of England?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-32#explanatio: Elizabeth was the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn. Since she never married, the Tudor dynasty ended with her in 1603.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-33#question: Which king sent the Armada against England in 1588?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-33#explanatio: Philip II wanted to overthrow Elizabeth I and restore Catholicism in England. The Armada was defeated by the English fleet and by storms.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-34#question: By what joint honorary title are Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon known?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-34#explanatio: The pope granted them the title in 1496. The couple united Spain, completed the Reconquista in 1492 and financed Columbus's voyage.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-35#question: Of which ruler was it said that the sun never set on his empire?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-35#explanatio: From 1519 Charles V united Spain and its colonies, the Netherlands, Naples, Austria and the imperial crown. He abdicated in 1556 and divided his realm.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-36#question: What was the alliance formed by Protestant princes and cities in 1531 called?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-36#explanatio: Princes such as Electoral Saxony and Hesse used it to defend their Reformation against the emperor. The Swabian League, by contrast, had crushed the rebellious peasants in 1525.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-37#question: In which city on India's Malabar Coast did Vasco da Gama land in 1498?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-37#explanatio: The new sea route around Africa bypassed Arab and Venetian middlemen. The Portuguese conquered Goa only in 1510.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-38#question: How many Africans in total were forcibly transported across the Atlantic to the Americas up to the 19th century?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-38#explanatio: The transatlantic slave trade began in the 16th century because the indigenous population of the Americas was dying in huge numbers. Portuguese, Spanish, English, French and Dutch traders took part in it.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-39#question: Who brought the only returning ship of Magellan's expedition back to Spain in 1522?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-39#explanatio: Magellan himself had been killed in the Philippines in 1521. Elcano brought the Victoria home with 18 survivors, completing the first circumnavigation of the globe.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-40#question: Which South American empire did Spanish conquerors under Francisco Pizarro destroy?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-40#explanatio: Pizarro exploited a civil war in the Inca Empire and captured the ruler Atahualpa in 1532. The Aztec Empire in Mexico had been conquered earlier by Cortés.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-41#question: What was the Spanish system called that gave colonists the right to force indigenous people to work?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-41#explanatio: The encomienda forced survivors to labour in mines and on plantations. Protective laws of 1542, obtained by Bartolomé de Las Casas, were barely enforced.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-42#question: What do historians call the sharp rise in prices in 16th-century Europe, to which American silver contributed?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-42#explanatio: After the discovery of the mines of Potosí and Zacatecas, hundreds of tonnes of silver flowed to Europe every year. Tulip mania and the Kipper und Wipper crisis, by contrast, belong to the 17th century.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-43#question: Which type of ship with triangular sails could tack against the wind and made the Portuguese voyages of discovery possible?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-43#explanatio: Together with the compass, astrolabe and cross-staff, the caravel allowed voyages far out into the open Atlantic. The cog, by contrast, was the typical ship of the Hanseatic League.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-44#question: Which crop reached Europe from the Americas as part of the Columbian Exchange?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-44#explanatio: Besides the potato, maize and tomatoes also came to Europe. In the other direction, Europeans brought wheat, horses and cattle to the Americas.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-45#question: Whose anatomy, handed down since antiquity, did Andreas Vesalius correct in 1543 through his own dissections?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-45#explanatio: Vesalius found more than 200 errors in Galen's teaching, which was based on dissections of animals. His De humani corporis fabrica appeared in the same year as Copernicus's main work.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-46#question: Which of these years is not a leap year under the rule of the Gregorian calendar?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-46#explanatio: Since 1582, full century years are leap years only if they are divisible by 400. That is why 1600 and 2000 were leap years, but 1900 was not.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-47#question: What is the name of Johannes Gutenberg's main work, completed around 1454?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-47#explanatio: The Gutenberg Bible was the first major printed book in Europe. Within fifty years, printing shops had sprung up in more than 250 European cities.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-48#question: To whom did Gutenberg lose his printing workshop because of his debts?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-48#explanatio: Gutenberg died without great wealth, but his invention spread rapidly across Europe. Fust carried on the printing business.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-49#question: Which 16th-century woman became famous as a painter?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-49#explanatio: Women were excluded from universities and most guilds, so artists such as Sofonisba Anguissola remained exceptions. Argula von Grumbach, by contrast, became known as a writer of the Reformation.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-50#question: Which Jesuit began the Christian mission in Japan in 1549?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-50#explanatio: Francis Xavier was one of the first companions of Ignatius of Loyola. The Jesuits did missionary work from Brazil to Japan and China, where Matteo Ricci later worked.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-51#question: Which of these events happened first?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-51#choices.1: The publication of Luther's Ninety-five Theses
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-51#choices.3: The consecration of Florence Cathedral with Brunelleschi's dome
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-51#explanatio: The cathedral was consecrated in 1436. Columbus landed in the Americas in 1492, Luther published his theses in 1517, and the Peace of Augsburg followed in 1555.
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-52#question: Which German painter became court painter to King Henry VIII of England?
q-renaissance-entdeckungen-52#explanatio: In London Holbein created famous portraits of the king and his court. Cranach, by contrast, was court painter to the Saxon electors and painted Luther.
q-revolutionen-01#question: Which event is regarded as the beginning of the French Revolution?
q-revolutionen-01#choices.3: The Battle of the Nations at Leipzig
q-revolutionen-01#explanation: The storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789 is regarded as the opening of the Revolution; July 14 is France's national holiday today.
q-revolutionen-02#question: Which colonies declared their independence from Great Britain in 1776?
q-revolutionen-02#choices.0: The Spanish colonies in South America
q-revolutionen-02#choices.3: Thirteen British colonies in North America
q-revolutionen-02#explanation: The thirteen colonies on the North American east coast founded the United States of America.
q-revolutionen-03#question: Who led the insurgents in the Haitian Revolution?
q-revolutionen-03#explanation: The former slave Toussaint Louverture became the most important leader of the uprising in Saint-Domingue.
q-revolutionen-04#question: What was the Code civil of 1804?
q-revolutionen-04#choices.2: A uniform civil code for France
q-revolutionen-04#explanation: The Code civil unified civil law and established equality before the law, property and freedom of contract.
q-revolutionen-05#question: Which statesman shaped the Congress of Vienna of 1814 to 1815 most decisively?
q-revolutionen-05#explanation: The Austrian foreign minister Metternich presided over the congress and stood for the policy of Restoration.
q-revolutionen-06#question: Why did the Frankfurt National Assembly fail in 1849?
q-revolutionen-06#choices.0: It could not agree on any basic rights
q-revolutionen-06#choices.3: The Prussian king refused the imperial crown
q-revolutionen-06#explanation: In 1849 Frederick William IV refused the imperial crown offered by the parliament; the National Assembly then fell apart.
q-revolutionen-07#question: In which city was the Constitution of the United States adopted in 1787?
q-revolutionen-07#explanation: From May to September 1787, 55 delegates deliberated on the constitution in Philadelphia under the chairmanship of George Washington; the capital Washington was not built until later.
q-revolutionen-08#question: What did the women of Paris achieve with their march to Versailles in October 1789?
q-revolutionen-08#choices.0: The right to vote for women
q-revolutionen-08#explanation: The women forced Louis XVI to sign the Declaration of the Rights of Man and to move with his family from Versailles to Paris, where he stood before the eyes of the people.
q-revolutionen-09#question: Which find from Napoleon's Egyptian campaign made the decipherment of the hieroglyphs possible?
q-revolutionen-09#explanation: The Rosetta Stone, found in 1799, bears the same text in hieroglyphs, demotic script and Greek; with it Champollion achieved the decipherment in 1822.
q-revolutionen-10#choices.1: Prussia lost the Battle of Jena
q-revolutionen-10#choices.2: The Confederation of the Rhine was founded
q-revolutionen-10#choices.3: Francis II laid down the crown of the Holy Roman Empire
q-revolutionen-10#explanation: After the founding of the Confederation of the Rhine and an ultimatum from Napoleon, Francis II declared the more than 800-year-old empire dissolved.
q-revolutionen-11#question: Whose arrival decided the Battle of Waterloo on the evening of June 18, 1815?
q-revolutionen-11#choices.0: The Russian Guard under Tsar Alexander
q-revolutionen-11#explanation: Wellington's army held out all day until Blücher's Prussians arrived and put Napoleon's army to flight.
q-revolutionen-12#question: Which work did Mary Wollstonecraft publish in 1792?
q-revolutionen-12#choices.0: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
q-revolutionen-12#choices.1: The Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen
q-revolutionen-12#explanation: In A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, Wollstonecraft demanded equal education and civil rights for women; the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen is the work of Olympe de Gouges.
q-revolutionen-13#question: Who drafted the American Declaration of Independence of 1776?
q-revolutionen-13#explanation: Thomas Jefferson of Virginia, then 33, wrote the line that all men are created equal. He later became the third president of the United States.
q-revolutionen-14#question: What position did the Code civil of 1804 give to married women?
q-revolutionen-14#choices.0: They received the right to vote for the National Assembly
q-revolutionen-14#choices.1: They were placed under the guardianship of their husbands
q-revolutionen-14#choices.2: They were made fully equal to men before the law
q-revolutionen-14#choices.3: They were allowed to manage the family property on their own
q-revolutionen-14#explanation: The Code civil guaranteed equality before the law for all men but placed married women under the authority of their husbands; they needed his consent for contracts and lawsuits, for example. The Revolution had already excluded women from politics in 1793.
q-revolutionen-15#question: What is the United States Bill of Rights of 1791?
q-revolutionen-15#choices.0: The first ten amendments to the Constitution, setting out basic rights
q-revolutionen-15#choices.1: The peace treaty with Great Britain after the War of Independence
q-revolutionen-15#choices.2: The law founding the capital city of Washington
q-revolutionen-15#choices.3: The declaration of independence from Great Britain
q-revolutionen-15#explanation: The ten amendments guaranteed freedom of speech, of the press and of religion, among other rights. They supplemented the Constitution of 1787, which had taken effect in 1789.
q-revolutionen-16#question: Under a compromise in the US Constitution of 1787, how were enslaved people counted when seats in the House of Representatives were apportioned?
q-revolutionen-16#choices.0: As three fifths of a person
q-revolutionen-16#choices.3: As one half of a person
q-revolutionen-16#explanation: The Three-Fifths Compromise strengthened the weight of the Southern states in Congress and entrenched slavery in the Constitution.
q-revolutionen-17#question: Who is regarded as the chief architect of the American Constitution of 1787?
q-revolutionen-17#explanation: James Madison shaped the deliberations in Philadelphia decisively and is often called the Father of the Constitution. Jefferson was serving as envoy in Paris at the time.
q-revolutionen-18#question: Against which state did Belgium rise up after the July Revolution of 1830 in Paris?
q-revolutionen-18#explanation: The Congress of Vienna had united the former Austrian Netherlands with the Netherlands. After the uprising of 1830 Belgium became an independent kingdom.
q-revolutionen-19#question: In which building did the first all-German parliament meet in 1848?
q-revolutionen-19#explanation: The Frankfurt National Assembly debated basic rights and an imperial constitution in St. Paul's Church. The building is regarded as the cradle of German democracy.
q-revolutionen-20#question: Which young Frenchman fought as a general alongside George Washington in the American War of Independence?
q-revolutionen-20#explanation: Lafayette sailed to America in 1777 at the age of 19 and contributed to the victory at Yorktown. In 1789 he presented the first draft of the Declaration of the Rights of Man to the National Assembly.
q-revolutionen-21#question: What step did the deputies of the Third Estate take in June 1789?
q-revolutionen-21#choices.0: They declared themselves the National Assembly
q-revolutionen-21#explanation: As they represented about 98 percent of the population, they claimed to speak for the whole nation. In the Tennis Court Oath they swore not to disband until France had a constitution.
q-revolutionen-22#question: Why did Louis XVI summon the Estates-General in 1789?
q-revolutionen-22#choices.0: He wanted to declare war on Austria
q-revolutionen-22#choices.1: He wanted a vote on his succession
q-revolutionen-22#choices.2: The state was facing financial bankruptcy

q-revolutionen-23#question: How many articles did the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen of August 26, 1789 contain?
q-revolutionen-23#explanation: Among other things, the 17 articles declared that all men are born free and equal in rights and that all sovereignty resides in the nation.
q-revolutionen-24#question: With which text did Olympe de Gouges respond to the Declaration of the Rights of Man in 1791?
q-revolutionen-24#choices.0: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
q-revolutionen-24#choices.1: Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen
q-revolutionen-24#explanation: She demanded the same rights for women as for men: if woman has the right to mount the scaffold, she must also have the right to mount the rostrum. She herself was executed in 1793.
q-revolutionen-25#question: What was the name of the agreement with which Napoleon was reconciled with the pope in 1801?
q-revolutionen-25#explanation: The Concordat recognized Catholicism as the religion of the majority of the French but kept the Church under state supervision. Church lands sold during the Revolution stayed with their new owners.
q-revolutionen-26#question: In which year was King Louis XVI executed?
q-revolutionen-26#explanation: After the fall of the monarchy in 1792 he was convicted of treason and guillotined on January 21, 1793. Queen Marie Antoinette followed him in October.
